best_for: PC and Steam Deck style Linux gamers who want to play their own Wii U games with higher resolutions and controller support.
description:
Cemu is a Wii U emulator from the Cemu project, written in C and C++ and still getting new features and fixes. On Windows you also need Microsoft's Visual C++ 2017 x64 redistributable, which the project links from its homepage.

The project's graphics advice is short. NVIDIA and AMD cards run as expected on a recent driver, but older AMD cards do badly with OpenGL. If your card has less than 2 GB of memory, choose OpenGL; otherwise Vulkan is the better pick. Motion controls use your controller's gyro if it has one, or you drag with the right mouse button instead. Fans also keep a collection of community graphic packs, and the project runs an official Discord.

points.title: Most Wii U games play
points.text: The project says Cemu runs most Wii U games and homebrew in a playable state. Check the compatibility wiki for the game you care about before you set things up.

points.title: Hardware it needs
points.text: Cemu needs 64-bit Windows 7 or later, a GPU with OpenGL 4.5 or Vulkan 1.2, and 4 GB of RAM, with 8 GB recommended. Intel graphics support is limited; Vulkan is the better choice there.

points.title: Controllers
points.text: It emulates the GamePad, Pro Controller and Classic Controller, works with keyboards and USB pads, and maps GamePad touch to the mouse. Wiimotes are only partly emulated.

points.title: Free and open source
points.text: Cemu has been open source under MPL 2.0 since version 2.0, with no paid edition.

points.title: Windows is a zip, macOS is experimental
points.text: The Windows build listed here is an x64 zip you extract, with no installer. The project calls its macOS build experimental with known slowdowns on Apple silicon, and this site does not list it. Windows keeps 8 versions.

points.title: Verified Flatpak on Linux
points.text: The Linux Flatpak is marked verified on Flathub for the Cemu Project and is x64 only. Only the current release is kept.
